name: climate
quote:
In semiarid
environments with inadequate water (< 1000 mm rainfall yr–1) and on acid
infertile soils, hedgerows produce too little biomass and/or become too
competitive to benefit crops. If (C) is substantially reduced, HI may increase
crop yields in some of these situations, even for a relatively small (F), but
the necessary management of hedges could be too intensive to be practical.
review_note: Scope includes the PDF page 15 discussion of slopes below 15%; this is not an executable slope limit. C means competition for resources and F means soil fertility. See units.json and independent_review.md.

name: acidsoil
quote:
In semiarid
environments with inadequate water (< 1000 mm rainfall yr–1) and on acid
infertile soils, hedgerows produce too little biomass and/or become too
competitive to benefit crops. If (C) is substantially reduced, HI may increase
crop yields in some of these situations, even for a relatively small (F), but
the necessary management of hedges could be too intensive to be practical.
On acid soils, HI may give a positive response over the long term and with
external inputs (lime and P fertilizer), but many small farmers may not cope
with these requirements.
review_note: Scope includes the PDF page 15 discussion of slopes below 15%; this is not an executable slope limit. C means competition for resources and F means soil fertility. See units.json and independent_review.md.

name: species_soil_selection
quote:
Leucaena and gliricidia are well suited for base-rich soils,
whereas calliandra, Acacia auriculiformis, peltophorum, dactyladenia, eryth-
rina, L. diversifolia and inga are suited for acid soils in specific climatic
conditions.
hold: Species-group scope:Leucaena/gliricidia base-rich;calliandra,A.auriculiformis,peltophorum,dactyladenia,erythrina,L.diversifolia,inga acid. Never generic practice pH.

name: fallow_species_nitrogen
quote:
The
issue of BNF may not be important for fallow species where the soils contain
large quantities of accumulated nutrients at depth or are inherently fertile
except for physical degradation. In these situations, tree species that efficiently
recycle nutrients from depth, improve soil physical and biological conditions
rapidly, and suppress weeds quickly are appropriate for use in tree fallows.
In nitrogen-depleted soils, however, species that have high BNF ability should
be preferred.
hold: BNF=biologicalnitrogenfixation; selectfunctionaltraits based nutrientdepletion. No genericfamilyassignment or inventedtaxon.
